conflicts: Throat: Juki Japan's Collector's Edition page and the Juki brochure diagram give an 'arm size' of 8.5 x 6 in, and jukiquilting.com gives no figure; dealers call 8.5 in throat space. Juki does not use the word throat or say the 8.5 in is measured needle to body, so we keep 8.5 in as the TL-family needle-to-body figure on the strength of dealer wording only, and it stays soft.
Weight: 25.4 lb (11.5 kg) on the Juki page and brochure, 24.5 lb on Juki Japan's page, 11.9 kg (about 26.2 lb) in the Juki manual. We show 25.4 lb.
Presser foot lift: the Juki page gives a lever lift of 10 mm, the Juki manual gives 7 mm. The knee lifter is 12 mm in both.
Hook: Juki's feature page says vertical full-rotary hook; Juki Japan's spec table says horizontal-axis full-rotary. We do not state an orientation.
Auxiliary table depth: 335 mm in one Juki document and 355 mm in another. We state neither.
Warranty: 2 years on motor and electrical parts and 5 years on other factory defects is Juki America's general FAQ wording, not text written for the TL-18QVP.
Max speed: the jukiquilting.com snippet reads 'Max. 15000 SPM', an evident typo; the Juki page speed slider and brochure say 1,500 spm. We use 1,500.
Price: Juki's suggested retail and the Amazon price differ, and jukiquilting.com tells buyers to contact an authorized Juki QVP dealer.

ownerThemes.theme: Owners who compared it with the TL-2010Q say there is not much difference other than price; the micro lift does not raise the foot much but is handy on very thick seams.
A retailer explainer frames the differences as more included feet and the micro lifter on the TL-18QVP, with the same 8.5 in throat and 1,500 spm on both machines.

editorial.verdict: A fast straight-stitch quilter on the TL-2010Q's 8.5 in throat; the extra buys a float function and nine feet, not more reach.
editorial.whoFor: A quilter or bag maker who wants a 1,500 spm straight-stitch machine, sews thick seams often, and values the float function and the included feet.
editorial.skipIf: You need any stitch other than straight, you want the TL-2010Q's same throat for less, or you want stitch regulation for frame quilting.

faqs.q: What do owners say about the Juki TL-18QVP?
faqs.a: Owners praise its speed and its power through thick layers such as vinyl bag panels, and several find the throat plentiful. Four owners call it very heavy. The repeated complaints are a walking foot that sheds black dust or shavings, thread trimmer limits (one owner says it handles only Tex 30 to 40 thread, and one unit's sensor cut at random) and an automatic threader that never worked for one owner. The read covers 41 first-hand voices from 32 Reddit threads, 2021 to 2026, and Reddit leans toward people asking for help, so problems are over-represented.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the TL-18QVP and the TL-2010Q?
faqs.a: Juki lists a float function (micro lifter) and an attachment mounting plate for the TL-18QVP and not for the TL-2010Q, and its brochure lists nine standard feet for the 18QVP. Owners say the 18QVP has nine feet against four on the 2010Q and better lighting, and Juki lists 4-step adjustable LED lighting for it. Juki lists $2,369 for the TL-18QVP and $2,169 for the TL-2010Q. One owner found the micro lifter not useful for bag making and recommends the 2010Q for that. Feet and lighting comparisons rest on owner comments and Juki pages, not a side-by-side test [verify].

faqs.q: What is the price of the Juki TL-18QVP?
faqs.a: Juki lists a suggested retail of $2,369 and tells buyers to contact an authorized Juki QVP dealer. Amazon showed $1,899 on 2026-10-01, so most buyers pay under list. Dealer prices vary with the kit, so check what is included before you compare. Prices drift weekly, so use the price band on this page as the stable guide.

faqs.q: What is the float function on the Juki TL-18QVP?
faqs.a: Juki describes it as a micro lifter: the presser foot floats 0 to 2 mm above the material. Owners are split. One uses it rarely, mostly for free motion quilting over very thick seams such as appliqué, another calls it occasionally useful with heavy leather, and a third found it not useful for bag making and says the TL-2010Q is the better recommendation.

faqs.q: How much throat space does the Juki TL-18QVP have?
faqs.a: Dealers give 8.5 in. Juki Japan's Collector's Edition page and the Juki brochure diagram give an 'arm size' of 8.5 x 6 in, jukiquilting.com gives no figure, and Juki does not say the 8.5 in is measured needle to body, so treat it as soft [verify]. The 23 in Juki lists is the work area with the auxiliary table attached, not throat space.

faqs.q: Is the Juki TL-18QVP a long-arm machine?
faqs.a: No. The 18 is a model designation, not inches. The 8.5 in figure is a domestic-class throat, well under the 16 to 18 in mid-arm range, and the 23 in work area depends on the auxiliary table.

faqs.q: How do you thread the Juki TL-18QVP, and does the needle threader work?
faqs.a: Juki lists an automatic needle threader, and owners are not fond of it: of the 3 voices who mention threading, 2 are negative. One owner never got it working and is considering a separate threader, another found the semi-automatic threader easy to use, and one notes the thread stand cannot be removed without taking off the side panel.

faqs.q: What feet and accessories come with the Juki TL-18QVP?
faqs.a: Juki lists nine presser feet: standard, hemming, zipper, even feed, 1/5 in and 1/4 in quilting, open-toe quilting, 1/4 in compensating and 1/4 in. It also lists a quilt guide, an auxiliary table and a knee lifter. One owner says neither this machine nor the TL-2010Q includes a free motion ruler foot or the narrow hinge foot, and owners report walking foot problems.

faqs.q: Can the Juki TL-18QVP go on a quilting frame?
faqs.a: Juki lists an attachment mounting plate for it, and owners describe a replaceable mounting plate on the right. The machine has no stitch regulator, so confirm frame fit and what you would control by hand with your dealer.
